fields.rt-blog-html:
With their lively atmosphere, tempting aromas and mouth-watering dishes, all your senses are on the alert: there's no doubt you're in a food hall. In Paris, in the regions or in the 4 corners of the globe, more and more of these places are attracting the curiosity of consumers and restaurateurs who see them as a great opportunity. Let's take a closer look at the world of these food halls, where culinary diversity, product quality and innovation come together to the delight of everyone who comes into contact with them. 

‍

Food court versus food hall 

Before we go any further, a few definitions are in order. A food court is a place that brings together a number of fast-food chains for whom speed of service is a priority. 

Food halls are catering spaces designed not only to delight customers' taste buds, but also to offer them a real experience. The food stands they house offer quality dishes, often made with fresh produce from short supply chains. These places promise a true gastronomic discovery. Artisanal spirit, authenticity and quality are all characteristics that distinguish food halls from food courts. 

👉 To find out more: Understanding the food court trend

‍

Food halls, a response to current consumer expectations 

To understand the proliferation of food halls and their popularity with consumers, it's important to analyze their needs and expectations. Today's French are constantly on the lookout for novelty and quality, both of which you'll find in a food hall. 

In fact, consumers are increasingly favoring local products, particularly for their taste (93% of French people), and are paying closer attention to their diet, aware of the impact it can have on their health. They demand complete transparency regarding the products they consume and prefer seasonal products from organic farming and short supply chains.

The French are also keen to discover new flavors. In a food hall, customers are free to flit from one stand to another, eating Asian, Italian and Lebanese dishes. 

Given these figures, it's easy to see why food halls are so popular. They are the perfect answer to today's consumer expectations , offering a pleasant, innovative setting and a wide choice of fresh produce prepared before their very eyes. 

‍

An interesting option for restaurateurs

While food halls are appealing to consumers, what about food service professionals? 

Increased visibility

Food halls are generally high-traffic areas. This high level of traffic offers increased visibility without the need to increase your marketing and communications budget. Customers visiting a competitor's restaurant or exploring the various food hall options will inevitably pass by your establishment and, who knows, maybe come back for you next time...

Cost sharing 

Sharing a space with other restaurateurs means you can reduce the costs of rental, fitting out and maintenance. So you can benefit from a high-quality infrastructure without having to bear the full cost. Personnel management, procurement and logistics are also considerably simplified. So you can concentrate more on the quality of your cuisine and the experience you offer your customers. 

A higher retention rate

Being present in a food hall not only demonstrates your ability to adapt to your customers' needs, but also your desire to offer them the best possible experience. Everything is designed to ensure that they have a pleasant time: a lively atmosphere, meticulous decor and a unique, high-quality meal. All this usually translates into increased customer loyalty. 

Boosted creativity

Food halls foster culinary innovation by encouraging restaurateurs to experiment with new concepts and adapt to market trends. Are you looking to develop your creativity, or do you believe it’s your strongest asset? Food halls will allow you to reach your full potential and gauge the public’s reaction to your new recipes. And why not collaborate with other professionals who have a stall near yours to create something even more original? 

‍

Key success factors for a food hall

The success of a fast food restaurant is based on a cocktail of several elements. The first key factor in the success of a food hall is the uniqueness of the location. This facilitates the development of a genuine storytelling that meets consumers' growing need for authenticity.  

To ensure the longevity of such a place, it's important to offer a high-quality, diversified and personalized catering service. The challenge is to achieve a perfect balance between elaborate and casual cuisine, built around fresh produce, all with complete transparency.

Finally, the third key element to a food hall’s success is the versatility of the venue. Consumers are increasingly drawn to holistic experiences! Combining culinary discovery with cultural elements will be highly appreciated. Hosting exhibitions, concerts, conferences, workshops, or even pop-up shops enriches the overall visitor experience and contributes to the venue’s vitality and ongoing appeal.

This list of criteria is far from exhaustive, but in our opinion they are the three essential ingredients for a successful food hall. 

‍

Tour de France of the best-known food halls 

Looking for inspiration to launch your own food hall or join one? Here are a few that are definitely worth checking out: 

  • Food Market, Paris and Lyon
  • La grande épicerie, Paris
  • Parisian Omnivore District (POD), Paris
  • La Halle Charolais, Paris
  • Les Halles de Lyon-Paul Bocuse, Lyon
  • Les Halles de Bacalan, Bordeaux
  • Les halles de la Major, Marseille
  • Galeries Lafayette Gourmet, Paris
  • Le Printemps du Goût, Paris

‍
